title: Smooth geometric stalks and coordinate-section closed fibres
statement:
Let $f:V\to S$ be smooth between locally Noetherian schemes. For compatible geometric points
$\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ and $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ with
$\bar v$ over $\bar s$, put $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ and
$B=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{V,\bar v}$. Use the canonical local ring map
$\varphi:A\to B$ induced by `strictHenselizationMap` and put
$\mathfrak m_A=\operatorname{maximalIdeal}(A)$ and
$\mathfrak m_B=\operatorname{maximalIdeal}(B)$. Then $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings,
$\varphi$ is flat and local, and $B/\mathfrak m_A B$ is regular. For every ideal
$I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$, the canonical quotient map $A/I\to B/IB$ is flat and local,
and its closed fibre is canonically $B/(IB+\mathfrak m_A B)\simeq B/\mathfrak m_A B$.

In the affine-space case, supply an isomorphism over $S$,
$e:V\simeq\mathbf A(\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin} r))_S$. For a finite subset
$K$ of the coordinate indices, let $t_i\in B$ be the image of
`AffineSpace.coord` under $\Gamma$ of the structural map followed by $e$. If
$t_i\in\mathfrak m_B$ for $i\in K$, then for every $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ the ring
$B/(IB+(t_i:i\in K))$ is Noetherian and local, its canonical map from $A/I$ is flat,
and its closed fibre is $F_K=B/(\mathfrak m_A B+(t_i:i\in K))$, which is regular; moreover
$\dim(B/\mathfrak m_A B)=\dim F_K+|K|$.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 01VF (lemma-smooth-flat), and Morphisms Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); Algebra Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization); More on Algebra Tag 06LN (lemma-henselization-regular) and Tag 06LK (lemma-henselization-dimension). Coordinate-fibre calculation uses Algebra Tag 00OR (lemma-dimension-height-polynomial-ring). These are the inputs to the agent-supplied strict-local comparison, rather than a claimed single theorem at one tag.

proof.text: Write $s,v$ for the images of the geometric points. Choose Noetherian affine neighbourhoods of $s$ and $v$, which exist by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] their ordinary local rings are prime localizations of the corresponding Noetherian coordinate rings, hence are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. The compatible affine-chart comparison [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] identifies $A$ and $B$ with the algebraic strict henselizations of these ordinary local rings, relative to the separable residue closures inside the common geometric field $\Omega$. Consequently [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] makes $A,B$ Noetherian. The same comparison says they are local and identifies their residue evaluations into $\Omega$ with their local residue maps. In particular, a function belongs to their maximal ideal exactly when its value under geometric-point evaluation is zero.

Let $j:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ be the strict-local structural map. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1), $\bar s$ factors through its closed geometric point $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Form $W=V\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\bar w=(\bar v,a)$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The projection $p:W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The structural map $j$ is ind-etale over an affine neighbourhood of $s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale]: it factors through that neighbourhood, since its inverse image contains the closed point of the local spectrum and therefore is the whole spectrum. The base-change clause of [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] now identifies $W_{(\bar w)}$ with $V_{(\bar v)}$. This is the canonical functorial identification. The ring map $A\to\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{W,\bar w}\cong B$ is the map $A\to B$ of the statement: it factors locally through the ordinary local ring at $w$ and its strict henselization by [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], its spectrum followed by $j$ is the structural map to $S$, and on residue fields it is the prescribed inclusion inside $\Omega$, so uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3) applies. These constructions use the same geometric field throughout.

source.place: Tag 08HV (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial-improve), scheme form; Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); ind-etale invariance as in Tags 05WR (lemma-quasi-finite-strict-henselization) and 0GIP (lemma-base-change-strict-henselization-quasi-finite).

proof.text: Let $w$ be the image of $\bar w$ and put $C=\mathcal O_{W,w}$. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] the smooth map $p$ is flat, so [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives a flat local map $A\to C$; here $w$ lies above the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose local ring is $A$ itself. The affine comparison [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] identifies $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{W,\bar w}$ with $C^{\mathrm{sh}}$ compatibly with its structural map. The local map $C\to C^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. Transitivity [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] makes $A\to C^{\mathrm{sh}}\cong B$ flat. It is local by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3), or by the composition of the two local maps. Notice that this flatness argument does not require $C$ to be Noetherian; it therefore applies unchanged to any smooth morphism at geometric points.

Put $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $Z=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$. This is a closed subscheme of $W$: on every affine chart with coordinate ring $D$, it is $\operatorname{Spec}(D/\mathfrak m_A D)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The point $\bar w$ factors through $Z$, since its map from $A$ factors through $\kappa$. By [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] its strict local ring is precisely $B/\mathfrak m_A B=F$, with the indicated quotient map. The morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). By the affine-local characterization in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], choose an affine neighbourhood of this point with smooth $\kappa$-algebra of functions. Its ordinary local ring is regular (and hence Noetherian) by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. Apply [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular] to obtain regularity of $F$. This argument for regularity of the strict-local closed fibre applies to any smooth morphism, independently of regularity of its base.

proof.text:
For $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat] applied to the flat $A$-module $B$ makes $B/IB$ flat over $A/I$. Since $A\to B$ is local, $IB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. The quotient-local-ring statement [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] gives maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A/I$ and $\mathfrak m_B/IB$ in the two nonzero quotients. The inverse image of the latter is the former: the residue of $a+I$ lies in it exactly when the image of $a$ in $B$ belongs to $\mathfrak m_B$, exactly when $a\in\mathfrak m_A$. Thus the induced map is local. Its closed fibre is
$$(B/IB)/(\mathfrak m_A/I)(B/IB)=B/\mathfrak m_A B=F,$$
since $IB\subseteq\mathfrak m_A B$. This proves the first paragraph of the statement.

proof.text: Now assume $V=\mathbf A^r_S$. Let $J_K=(t_i:i\in K)$ and let $V_K\hookrightarrow V$ set these coordinates equal to zero. On an affine base chart its coordinate-ring quotient sends the selected variables to zero and fixes every other variable; its inverse identifies it with the polynomial ring in the remaining $r-k$ variables. These maps commute with restriction to principal opens, so [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] identifies $V_K=\mathbf A^{r-k}_S$ over $S$. It is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its projection is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. The evaluation statement in step 1 and $t_i\in\mathfrak m_B$ imply that $\bar v$ factors through $V_K$. By [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] its strict local ring is $B_K=B/J_K$. Applying the argument of steps 2--3 to the smooth projection $V_K\to S$ gives a flat local map $A\to B_K$. Here this repeats that argument with $V_K$ in place of $V$, not an appeal to the conclusion of this item. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], as in step 5, $A/I\to B_K/IB_K=B/(IB+J_K)$ is flat and local. This quotient is Noetherian: each of its ideals lifts to an ideal of the Noetherian ring $B$, whose finite generators descend to generators of the original ideal. Its closed fibre is $B/(\mathfrak m_A B+J_K)=F/(\bar t_i:i\in K)=F_K$.

source.place: Tags 00T6 (definition-standard-smooth), 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth), 01VF (lemma-smooth-flat), 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization), 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change); coordinate quotient from the polynomial universal property.

proof.text: In the model of step 2, the affine fibre of $W=\mathbf A^r_A$ over the closed point is $\operatorname{Spec}P$ with $P=\kappa[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$. This follows from the affine description in [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] and the tensor-product description [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]: evaluating the coefficients in $\kappa$ gives the polynomial ring over $\kappa$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be the prime defined by the lifted geometric point in this fibre. Then every $t_i$ for $i\in K$ lies in $\mathfrak q$. Put $L=(t_i:i\in K)\subset P$ and $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q/L$. Step 4 and [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] identify $F$ with $(P_{\mathfrak q})^{\mathrm{sh}}$. The closed-immersion quotient statement [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian], now for $\operatorname{Spec}(P/L)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}P$, similarly identifies $F_K$ with $((P/L)_{\mathfrak q'})^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Here $P/L$ is the polynomial ring in the remaining variables, by sending those variables to their quotient classes and all selected variables to zero. The localizations of $P$ and $P/L$ are Noetherian regular local rings by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring]; their strict henselizations are regular by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular]. In particular $F_K$ is regular.

Let $D=\kappa[t_i:i\in K]\subset P$ and $\mathfrak n=(t_i:i\in K)\subset D$. Since $\mathfrak q$ contains the selected variables, $\mathfrak q\cap D=\mathfrak n$: reduction of any $f\in D$ modulo those variables is its constant in $\kappa$, and a nonzero constant is a unit, so cannot belong to $\mathfrak q$. Both $D$ and $P$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring]. The map $D\to P$, adjoining the other variables, is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] and flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] at $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak n$:
$$\dim P_{\mathfrak q}=\dim D_{\mathfrak n}+\dim(P_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak nP_{\mathfrak q}).$$
The first summand is $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-origin-regular-local]. The second ring is $(P/L)_{\mathfrak q'}$: the two maps send $f/g$ to $(f\bmod L)/(g\bmod L)$ and conversely, and denominators are invertible on both sides. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension] and the models in step 7, $\dim F=\dim P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\dim F_K=\dim(P/L)_{\mathfrak q'}$. Hence $\dim F=\dim F_K+k$. The argument includes $K=\varnothing$ (then $D=\kappa$, $\mathfrak n=0$) and $K=\{1,\ldots,r\}$; it never assumes $\mathfrak q$ maximal.

(2) The strict-local structural map is ind-etale over an affine chart, because an open containing the closed point of a local spectrum is everything. The base-change clause of lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance gives W_(w) = V_(v), and uniqueness in functoriality (3) gives the A-structure. statement_change.old_statement:
Let $v:V\to S$ be a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Choose a geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$ and its image $\bar s$ in $S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $A=\mathcal O_{S,\bar s}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}$ be the strict local rings, namely the geometric stalks of the etale structure sheaves [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Then $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings and $A\to B$ is a flat local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The closed fibre $F=B/\mathfrak m_A B$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$, the map $A/I\to B/IB$ is flat and local, and has the same closed fibre $F$.

There is also the following coordinate form. Suppose $V=\mathbf A^r_S$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], with coordinates $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, and let $K\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ be any subset for which $t_i\in\mathfrak m_B$ for all $i\in K$. Put $k=|K|$. Then for every ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ the ring $B/(IB+(t_i:i\in K))$ is Noetherian and local, its map from $A/I$ is flat, and its closed fibre is $F_K=F/(\bar t_i:i\in K)$. Moreover $F_K$ is regular and
$$\dim F=\dim F_K+k,$$
where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].
